neighbours.label: The token ' a' right after a verb of giving, awarding or assigning, where a rating, score or mark is expected next (given a ..., awarded it a ...)
fire: Each restaurant in the guide is visited twice and given a score out of ten.
The teacher read my report and gave it a mark of seven.
Inspectors toured the factory and awarded it a rating of good.
Every wine in the tasting was assigned a grade by the panel.
The referee watched the routine and gave her a nine.
Films on the site are each given a star rating by readers.
After the audit the school was awarded a pass with merit.
Reviewers tried the phone for a week and gave it a rating of four stars.
quiet: Each restaurant in the guide is visited twice and has a page of its own.
The teacher read my report and found a mistake on page seven.
Inspectors toured the factory and noticed a leak in the roof.
Every wine in the tasting came from a farm near the coast.
The referee watched the routine and wrote a note in her book.
Films on the site are each shown with a short trailer for readers.
After the audit the school built a library with new shelves.
Reviewers tried the phone for a week and found a scratch on the screen.

notes: 17 of the top 32 card examples peak on ' a', after give/given, and the - pole's output promotes ' pass', ' success', ' star', ' completion'. Probes: given a rating 1.04, awarded it a score 0.91, assigned a grade 0.91, give the student a check 0.41; ' a' after 'saw' 0.01. A giving verb with an unrelated object still fired 0.37 ('give the student a sandwich'), so the verb frame carries part of it and the expected rating adds the rest; near misses here use ' a' after other verbs.
